_what: How schematics/ore_plant.nbt was cut out of the server world. Replay with tools/world_clip.py --spec. The world files themselves are not in the repository (scratch/ is ignored); tools/pull-world-region.sh fetches them again.
_where: games2.geraldhofbauer.net:25567, the ore processing plant Gerry was standing in front of at -3294.8 / 8.8 / -2122.2.
_box:
A flood fill is useless here: the machine is built inside a deepslate-brick room, and the kinetic network runs on into the next machine, so 'everything connected that was placed by hand' is the entire base. The box is the cluster of ore-processing blocks, measured rather than eyeballed.

The north edge sits at -2141 rather than at -2139, where the machinery appears to stop. Two blocks further north stand a water wheel and the gearbox it turns, and that gearbox is what drives the washing fan. Cut at -2139 the fan arrives with no power at all, and nothing about the schematic would say so.

The east edge sits at -3289, one block past the docking station, and that is deliberate. The cluster runs on to -3280, but what continues there is 108 item vaults, 85 deployers, 54 drills, 16 chassis, a cart assembler and a plough — the mining train from the pilot episode, parked at its unloading point. Cutting at the cluster boundary would have put 142 of its blocks in the schematic and left 132 outside, which is how ten unexplained deployers and a vault wall with no purpose ended up in the first cut.

boxes._what: the plant. The top edge is at 17 rather than 15, which is two blocks of empty stone for the sake of one block of water: the wheel that drives the display board sits at 15 with its source directly above it, and cut at 15 the wheel arrives dry and the wall never flips a flap.

the boiler that drives it: five tank columns on magma, five steam engines on top, five pumps feeding them, and the water wheels that turn the pumps. Its own box, because the forty blocks of corridor between the two are empty and paving them costs five hundred blocks of floor nobody films.

_drop: The housing. 1026 of the 1397 built blocks in the box are the room the machine stands in, and an episode that builds them is an episode that spends two minutes on a wall. Every id is listed rather than matched by pattern, because '_slab' would also throw away something that turns out to matter.
_keep: Deliberately kept even though they look like scenery: redstone_block and redstone_lamp drive the stockpile switch and the content observers, chests and barrels are the machine's own buffers, and the rail, plough and cart assembler belong to the vault bank that docks on portable storage interfaces.
_machine: One block of oak leaves, at local (8,4,2), directly in front of the washing fan. It is waterlogged, and that water is the entire reason the fan washes anything — Create reads the fluid state, not the block. Leaves are worldgen everywhere else in this world, so without naming it here the clip drops it and the washing stage arrives as a fan pointed at nothing. It is the only waterlogged natural block anywhere near the machinery, so nothing else comes with it.
_clearContainers: Emptied on the way out. The plant had been running for a while and its chests held 1365 quartz, 444 experience nuggets and 299 lapis — the source machine's takings. The bill of materials counts items inside block entities (that is how the pilot's deployers arrive with their filters), so leaving them in would put the whole warehouse in the materials chest and call it a building cost. Filters live in their own key and are untouched.
_support: Dropping the room a machine is built into leaves the machine hanging in the air, and the verifier does not catch it: it looks immediately after placement, before the block updates that make an unsupported block fall have propagated. So the housing comes back where it is holding something up — the block underneath, and the wall behind anything mounted on one. Not a full six-sided shell: the first attempt at that walled in the front of the machine too, and the camera spent a whole orbit looking at a bunker. Fluids get more than that: every water block and every waterlogged block is boxed in on all six sides, because water that is not held flows, and flowing water is gone by the next check. That rule is what keeps the leaf block in front of the washing fan wet.
_origin: Declared, not derived. Local coordinates are what the parts manifest and every cue in the storyboard are written against, and letting the corner follow the selection renumbers all of them whenever the cut changes — which happened three times before this line existed. A block outside it is an error now, not a silent shift.
_resetStates: Block states that a world computes rather than a player chooses. Redstone wire carries its signal strength in its own blockstate, and a cloned wire arrives frozen at whatever it was carrying on the server — so the clutch downstream reads fifteen and stays disengaged no matter what the lever does, and the plant never starts. Same for the clutch's own powered flag and the lamps. Set them to the resting value and let the world work them out from the sources it can actually see.
_clearNbtKeys: Cached kinetic state, dropped on the way out. A Create block entity saves the network it belongs to — id, size, stress, capacity — and the speed it was turning at. Cloned, every wheel and shaft arrives certain it belongs to a network that exists on another machine: the water wheel spins, because it is a source, and drives nothing, because what it thinks it is driving is not here. It looks like a Create bug and it is a stale cache. Same family as the redstone wire's power and the content observer's powered flag.
